SMTO-HTTP-0069 — The request's data is nested too deeply

GUID: ec8719bf-cb30-4580-8950-b18b26ec00bf
Slug: http-json-depth-limit
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The data in this request has more than 64 layers of groups inside groups, which is more than SMTO will send. Nothing was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to simplify the data so it has fewer layers, following the format shown in the service's documentation. Most services expect data only a few layers deep, so a simpler shape is usually what they want anyway.
  2. If you're sending many related items, ask the Agent to split them into several smaller requests, or use the service's batch option if it has one. Smaller requests each stay well within SMTO's limit.

What success looks like

  • The Agent's request is sent and returns a result from the service.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete saved data to work around this; the limit is about the shape of this one request.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Body validation found JSON or form data nested more than 64 levels deep.

What this means

  • Recursive JSON/body validation descended beyond 64 levels. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Recursive JSON/body validation descended beyond 64 levels.

How to diagnose it

  • Measure nesting depth rather than total bytes; changing model context does not change this validation bound.

How to fix it

  • Flatten the payload to 64 nesting levels or fewer while keeping the endpoint's expected structure, or split it into several requests using the provider's supported batch format.
  • Reduce nesting while preserving the endpoint contract, or split the request using the provider-supported batch format.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The endpoint-compatible payload remains within 64 nesting levels.

What not to do

  • Do not erase authoritative receipts or protected current input to conceal a size/capacity problem.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
